rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and 3 - the authors report their own airborne hyperspectral and thermal campaigns over 27 olive orchards in Spain and Italy, field disease assessments of >14,000 trees confirmed by PCR, and their own three-stage machine learning classification results (sensitivity/specificity tests, Figs. 10-11).
rows.notes: The study reports detection and discrimination of Xylella fastidiosa versus Verticillium dahliae infections in olive trees using airborne thermal and hyperspectral traits (OA 92-98%, kappa 0.7-0.8, FP rates 4-9%). It does not report any result on controlling, eradicating or limiting the expansion of Xf; control/eradication is only mentioned as a motivation in the introduction and discussion. Detection is a precondition of the claimed control function, so Q2 is 'no' and upstream is true. Note also that the study discriminates symptomatic (DS>=1) from asymptomatic trees rather than demonstrating previsual detection; early-stage detection is listed as future work.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Supplementary Table S1 (list of narrow-band indices) not included but not needed for rating.
